summary: Adapted the complete implementation from the existing open upstream candidate PR 36136 onto the prepared newer main base. The opt-in DFLASH_CONFIDENCE algorithm adds selected-path survival confidence (trained head with STS calibration or selector-lattice fallback), SPS cost-table budget selection, per-request prefix allocation, compact ragged target verification with graph-token buckets, observability/profiling, and compatibility gating. Static DFLASH remains the default. Unit, compatibility, adversarial scheduling, and ROCm GPU kernel-reference tests pass. End-to-end model serving remains unverified because no compatible DFlash2 target/draft weights were available; the deterministic tiny Llama fixture is not architecture-qualified for this feature.

tests.what_was_measured: 70 tests and 18 subtests covering confidence extraction, selected-path survival, STS, SPS budget selection, graph-tier alignment, lossless cutoff/bonus behavior, static compatibility, and adversarial invalid inputs.
26 tests and 3 subtests covering ragged layout geometry/backend capability plus existing DFlash overlap and buffer compatibility.
One GPU test with 22 parameterized subtests comparing the modified verify-window/cutoff kernels on an AMD Instinct MI355X against independent PyTorch numerical references.
Python syntax compilation and patch whitespace validity.
Unavailable in the pinned interpreter: No module named ruff. No package installation or stack mutation was attempted.

gpu_execution.evidence: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 exposed exactly one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) under torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015; the 22 GPU numerical-reference subtests passed. See gpu-info.log and gpu-kernel-parity.log.

remaining_limitations: No compatible DFlash2 target/draft checkpoint was supplied or locally cached, so end-to-end HTTP serving, real confidence-head checkpoint loading, CUDA/HIP graph replay in a live engine, quality equivalence, and throughput were not rerun on this node.
The qualified tiny Llama fixture was intentionally not used because it validates transport/engine execution only and cannot qualify the DFlash2 architecture or semantics.

The implementation originated in still-open upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36136 and was adapted to the newer prepared base; upstream CI for that PR is not treated as evidence here.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so native_rebuilt is false and no native rebuild was applicable.
Ruff is absent from the pinned interpreter; compileall, git diff --check, and focused tests were used without modifying the software stack.
